title: 10 Pesos

composition.text: Bimetallic: nickel silver centre in aluminium bronze ring (Core: 65% Copper, 10% Nickel, 25% Zinc - Ring: 92% Copper, 6% Aluminium, 2% Nickel)

obverse.description: The national arms of Mexico (an eagle on cactus facing left with a snake in beak above wreath) with the inscription forming a semicircle above.

reverse.description: In the center there is the circle of the Aztec sun stone representing Tonatiuh with the fire mask. In the peripheral ring at top center the value; to the left the mint year, and to the right the mark of the Mint of Mexico "Mo"; at the bottom, the face value in words. On most coins the inverted "L' shape ornament along the rim. See comments for details.

comments:
A few main groups of dies are known.

 

Obverse
Die 1 - bold font, high knot in bow of the wreath, tip of laurel leaf to the center of "S" in MEXICANOS.
Die 2 - fine font, high knot in bow of the wreath, tip of laurel leaf to the bottom of "S" in MEXICANOS.
Die 3 - fine font, squat knot in bow of the wreath, tip of laurel leaf to the center of "S" in MEXICANOS..
Die 4 - fine font, high knot in bow of the wreath, tip of laurel leaf to the top of "S" in MEXICANOS.
Note. There are many more differences between dies, above are mentioned those for easy attribution.

Picture: © Images courtesy of Alexandr Prokofyev.

 

Reverse 
1998
Die A - date far from left denticle.
Die B - date close to the left denticle.

Picture: © Images courtesy of Alexandr Prokofyev.

 

2007
Die A - top of denticles clockwise as on model 1997 (see photo on the image in description of the Obverse dies 3+A).
Die B - top of denticles counterclockwise.

On the image below the die A  is on the left and the die B is on the right. Spanish speaking collectors nicknamed the die B grafila invertida.

 

Combinations
Die 1: 1997, 1998 (1+A, 1+B), 1999, 2002, 2004.
Die 2: 2005.
Die 3: 2006, 2007 (3+A, 3+B), 2008-2010.
Die 4: 2011-2018, 2021.
